newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia sees 1997 inflation at 13 pct - report.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia sees 1997 inflation at 13 pct - report.

text.p: The Yugoslav government expects to cut inflation to 13 percent in 1997 from an estimated 60 percent this year, the Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce said in a report obtained by Reuters on Wednesday.
The gross domestic product (GDP) growth was projected to reach 10-13 percent and public spending to account for 46.6-48 percent of that figure, the chamber of commerce said.

October inflation, measured by the retail price index (RPI) grew 1.4 percent on September. Year-on-year RPI was 69.6 percent. Cummulative January-October inflation stood at 49.2 percent on December 1995.
Government statistics estimated inflation in December to range between 50 and 60 percent year-on-year compared with 120 percent in 1995.
Analysts said such forecasts were too optimistic.
An independent Belgrade Economics Institute revised its 1996 forecast upwards from 85 to 95 percent because of high inflatory expectations.
